title: Multi-armed bandits: post-test
note: Two forms of five, asked in a fixed order (2026-11-05, Phil's items and Andrii's merged): understanding greedy, greedy's lock-in, UCB's rule, one UCB round, a changed UCB. Form A: T1 (greedy after a lucky start), T12 (lock-in from a small dip, Phil's), T16 (why UCB picked a lower average: V5's inverse), T4 (one round, the bonus formula not given, every option a set), T6 (a bonus that stops growing). Form B, the twins in new settings: V11, V15, V13, V14, V4. No anchor. Every other item (the team's T1 to T10 and V1 to V10, the ε-greedy ones, Phil's T10, T11, T13 and T14, the optimistic start T15 with its twin V12) is in stash/exercises.json, kept with its key and notes, never served.

items.title: Canteens
items.prompt: A team chooses among three canteens with greedy and scores each lunch out of 10. The true averages, unknown to the team, are A 7, B 6 and C 4, and most lunches score within 1 point of their canteen's true average. On the three trial days each canteen is tried once: A scores 6.5, B has an exceptionally good lunch and scores 9, and C scores 4. Where does the team eat on most days of the following year?
options: At B
At A
At A and B, about equally often
It depends on whether B has more exceptional lunches
items.explain: Greedy first picks B, which has the highest average. B keeps being tried, and its lunches of about 5 to 7 pull its average towards 6. After about 7 lunches it falls below A's 6.5, and greedy switches to A. A's average settles near 7, above B's, which no longer changes.
items.rubric: B keeps being tried, so its too-high average falls below A's; A then stays ahead.
diagnosis: Kai: F4 (greedy commits after the first tries)
correct
learner: greedy alternates when averages are close
learner: the outcome is down to luck
items.note: In 2,000 simulated years greedy ate at A on 97% of days.

items.title: Study spots
items.prompt: A student picks one of two study spots each evening with greedy and rates each evening's focus out of 10. Spot A is truly better: its evenings usually score between 7 and 9. Spot B's evenings always score between 6 and 7. On the two trial evenings, A scores 5.5, a bit below its usual, and B scores 6.5. What does greedy do for the rest of the term?
options: It switches between A and B for a while, since their averages are close
It goes back to A once B's average drops a little
It never picks A again, all term
It goes back to A after a while, once A's average has corrected itself
items.explain: After the trials B leads, 6.5 to 5.5, so greedy picks B. Every evening at B scores at least 6, so B's average never drops below 6, which stays above A's 5.5. A is never picked again, so its 5.5 is never corrected: a first try only a little below its usual is enough to lock greedy out of the better spot.
items.rubric: B's average can't fall below A's 5.5 (B never scores below 6); A isn't picked again, so its average is never corrected.
diagnosis: learner: greedy alternates when averages are close
learner: overlooks that B never scores below 6, so B's average can't fall below 5.5
correct
Kai: F5 (averages correct themselves, so greedy finds the best in the end)
items.note: New 2026-11-05 (ε-greedy left the lesson), in t03's place. Lock-in from a small dip rather than a disaster, with a bound to check: a step past Kai's lock-in question, easier than t01 (a too-high start that corrects itself). The key follows from the bounds; no simulation needed. "Never picks A again" can also come from Kai's F4 belief (greedy commits after the first tries): the reason tells them apart.

items.title: Inverse
items.prompt: In round 200, UCB picks B, although A has a higher average than B. Which must be true?
options: B was last picked longer ago than A
B's last reward was above its average
B's rewards have varied more than A's
B has been tried fewer times than A
items.explain: UCB picks the highest average plus bonus, so B's score was at least as high as A's. B's average is lower, so B's bonus must be larger. Both bonuses belong to round 200, so they differ only through the tries: a larger bonus means fewer tries.
items.rubric: B's bonus must exceed A's; in the same round that means fewer tries.
diagnosis: learner: the bonus depends on how long ago an option was picked
learner: the bonus reacts to recent results
Kai: F14 (the bonus adapts to the observed rewards)
correct
items.note: T12 until the merge with Phil's items (2026-11-05); moved from form B (V5): UCB's rule understood, no calculation. Option (a) is tempting because an unpicked bonus grows, but all bonuses use the same round number, so only the tries differ.

items.title: Recipes
items.prompt: A recipe app suggests one of four recipes with UCB. All of the following is for the same round. The bonus formula and its setting are not given: compare the recipes by their averages and how often each was tried. Recipe A averages 7.2 (80 tries), B 6.5 (6 tries), C 7.2 (120 tries) and D 5.0 (6 tries). Which recipes could UCB suggest next?
options: A or B
A or C
B or D
Any of the four
items.explain: UCB picks the highest average plus bonus, and within one round fewer tries means a larger bonus. A beats C: the same average, fewer tries. B beats D: the same tries, a higher average. A against B depends on the sizes of the bonuses, which are not given.
items.rubric: Rules out C and D by these comparisons; A against B cannot be decided.
diagnosis: correct
learner: the best average wins, as with greedy (ties broken by the averages alone)
Kai: F9 (picks the fewest tries)
learner: without the bonus values any option could win
items.note: Rewritten 2026-11-05: the bonus formula is said not to be given, and every option names a set of recipes (none a single one), so the item asks which comparisons the tries settle and which they don't.

items.title: A bonus that stops growing
items.prompt: A developer simplifies UCB: the bonus still shrinks each time an option is tried, but it no longer grows with the round number. There are two options. A is truly better (average 8) and has been tried 5 times, but its rewards so far were unusually low, and its score (average plus bonus) is now 5.5. B has been tried 40 times, and its rewards always lie between 6 and 7. What does the simplified UCB do from now on?
options: It picks A in the next round
It picks A again after a while
It picks A again once B's bonus has shrunk enough
It never picks A again
items.explain: UCB picks the higher score, now B's, which is at least B's average, so at least 6. A is not picked, so its average and its tries stay the same, and in this version its bonus does not grow either: A's score stays at 5.5. B's score never falls below 6, so A is never picked again, the same lock-in as with greedy.
items.rubric: A's score is frozen; B's score stays above it.
diagnosis: Kai: F9 (picks the fewest tries)
learner: answers for ordinary UCB and ignores the change
learner: overlooks that B's average alone beats 5.5
correct

items.title: Commute routes
items.prompt: A commuter chooses among three routes to work with greedy and rates each trip out of 10. The true averages, unknown to the commuter, are A 6, B 8 and C 5, and most trips score within 1 point of their route's true average. On the three trial days each route is tried once: A has an exceptionally good trip and scores 9, B scores 7.5, and C scores 5. Which route does the commuter take on most days of the year?
options: Route A
Routes A and B, about equally often
Route B
It depends on whether A has more exceptional trips
items.explain: Greedy first picks A, which has the highest average. A keeps being tried, and its trips of about 5 to 7 pull its average down. After two or three trips it falls below B's 7.5, and greedy switches to B. B's average settles near 8, above A's, which no longer changes.
items.rubric: A keeps being tried, so its too-high average falls below B's; B then stays ahead.
diagnosis: Kai: F4 (greedy commits after the first tries)
learner: greedy alternates when averages are close
correct
learner: the outcome is down to luck
items.note: The twin of T1 (2026-11-05): a lucky start on a worse route and a slightly low start on the best one, in another setting.

items.title: Forever
items.prompt: UCB runs forever on four options. Option D is clearly the worst, and by round 10,000 UCB's averages show this. How does UCB treat D from then on?
options: D is picked again only if its average rises
After some round, D is no longer picked
D keeps being picked, with ever longer gaps
D is picked at a roughly fixed share of rounds
items.explain: While D is not picked, its bonus keeps growing with the round number, without limit. So D's score eventually beats the best option's, and D is picked again. Each pick shrinks D's bonus, and the regrowth gets ever slower, so each gap is longer than the last.
items.rubric: The bonus of an unpicked option grows without limit; each pick shrinks it, and regrowth slows.
diagnosis: learner: UCB treated like greedy
Kai: F11 (an unpicked bonus stays the same), or F10 (every bonus shrinks over time)
correct
Kai: F11 vague (the bonus grows at a steady rate)
items.note: The twin of T6 (2026-11-05): both ask how an option the averages show to be worse fares from then on, T6 under a changed bonus, V4 under ordinary UCB.
